messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: Incident detected — spike in 5xxs from EU regions for inference-api (geo routing failures). Rolling 5m error rate at 18% vs baseline 0.6%. Auto-page sent to on-call.
Jamie (on-call): saw it, acking. digging into geodns path now. @Raj can you stand by for a possible handoff?
Jamie (on-call): quick summary: multiple customers reporting elevated errors and timeouts. Traces point to DNS resolution inconsistencies — some EU nodes resolving to stale origin IPs/old edge set. TCP connects to those IPs are failing.
Raj Patel: on my way. can you paste the SLO page and the short query / curl that shows the bad response?
Jamie (on-call): pasting sample:
```
$ dig +short @8.8.8.8 inference.eu.redwood.example
192.0.2.45
# this one is the stale record (should be 198.51.100.12)
```
and from another resolver:
```
$ dig +short @1.1.1.1 inference.eu.redwood.example
198.51.100.12
```
So resolvers return different A records depending on upstream provider. TTLs are 300s right now.
Maria Gomez: tagging support — are customers noticing request failures or higher latencies only? we need to triage impact level for comms.
Jamie (on-call): primary impact = 5xx (gateway/connect), some retries succeed when resolver returns the healthy IP. Affected customers: small subset on EU region, roughly 12 customers, 3 with production traffic. Current mitigation candidates: 1) lower TTL and force a global refresh, 2) flip geodns fallback order to prefer route53 endpoints, 3) add temporary synthetic CNAME that points to healthy pool. Thinking 1+2 immediately.
Kevin Liu: agree. Lower TTL first to 30s to reduce propagation time. I'm prepping the route53 change now.
Raj Patel: I'm going to take the pager; Jamie can you announce handoff? I'll coordinate DNS changes and hit Cloudflare support in parallel.
Jamie (on-call): handing off to Raj — I'm shifting to post-incident doc. Raj, you're primary. :white_check_mark:
Raj Patel: ack — taking lead. Kevin, please share the CLI you plan to run for TTL change.
Kevin Liu: running this from infra-admin (dry-run logged):
```
# update Cloudflare DNS TTL via API (simplified)
curl -X PATCH "https://api.cloudflare.com/client/v4/zones/$ZONE/dns_records/$RECORD" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $CF_TOKEN" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  --data '{"ttl":30}'
```
I'll then submit Route53 change to make fallback prefer the healthy pool.
Support Bot: Escalation note created: INC-2026-1834. CS notified for impacted accounts; outreach queue populated.
Raj Patel: TTL lowered to 30s (confirmed via dig after ~40s from multiple resolvers). Now updating geodns policy: swapping fallback order to route53-first for eu-healthy pool. Making change via control-plane.
incident-bot: deploybot: config-change: geodns-policy updated by raj.patel — policy version 488 -> 489 (rollback window 15m).
Maria Gomez: any visible improvement in error rate?
Raj Patel: within 5 minutes error rate dropped from 18% -> 4.2%. Some customers still see intermittent failures due to cached resolvers.
Jamie (on-call): good. let's keep monitoring for 30m. Please open a ticket with Cloudflare with traces and ask for an explanation for inconsistent resolver responses — include sample dig outputs.
Kevin Liu: Cloudflare ticket # open, SR-987654, link pasted in incident doc. They acknowledge and are investigating regional resolver cache misalignment.
Raj Patel: rolling monitoring checklist: 1) confirm full recovery across EU POPs (done for most), 2) run synthetic checks from major public resolvers (8.8.8.8, 1.1.1.1, local ISP), 3) set TTL back to 300 once stabilized.
Support Bot: Customer impact summary (short): ~12 customers affected, 3 in prod — transient 5xxs for 2-8 minutes depending on cache expiry. No data loss. CS ping scheduled for 10:00 UTC.
Jamie (on-call): note for post-incident: evaluate reducing default TTL for geodns records pre-emptively, add resolver-consistency checks to Canary tests, and add an automated fallback that switches routing order when resolver variance > threshold.
Raj Patel: rolling TTL back to 300 now. Will keep 15m observation window.
incident-bot: monitor: error-rate EU inference-api = 0.9% (moving 5m). rolling to steady state.
Maria Gomez: thanks team — created follow-up ticket in backlog: GEO-42 (add resolver-consistency alert and auto-failover). Assigning to eng-runtime and eng-sre.
Raj Patel: closing handoff. I'll write the timeline and RCA draft. tagging @Kevin for the Cloudflare SR notes.
Jamie (on-call): leaving final note: no customer-facing incident banner needed — CS will reach out to the three affected customers. Great fast work. :tada:
note: This thread is a single Slack conversation from incident detection through mitigation and handoff. All messages are in chronological order and prefixed with sender names as required.
